content:
Reason for Testing: Whole-Genome Sequencing Diagnostic Test provided by NHS GMS
Patient was tested as part of a trio via whole-genome sequencing provided by the NHS Genomic Medicine Service (GMS) to investigate the cause of their daughter’s clinical presentation. He is stated to be clinically unaffected. Daughter is homozygous for a pathogenic MPDZ nonsense variant (see accompanying WGS Viapath Genetics report dated 06/10/2022). 

	
Result Summary 
Familial heterozygous MPDZ variant detected 




Result
Patient is a CARRIER of the familial pathogenic MPDZ variant detected in his daughter.

Implications of result
These results indicate that both parents are carriers of the familial pathogenic MPDZ variant.  The risk that their next pregnancy will be affected with autosomal recessive Hydrocephalus, congenital 2 with or without brain or eye anomalies (MIM #615219) is 1 in 4 (25%). 

Prenatal testing is possible for this couple and pre-implantation diagnosis may be an option.                       We recommend that this is discussed with Clinical Genetics prior to testing.

If appropriate, testing can be offered to other family members. We recommend that they are referred to Clinical Genetics to discuss this prior to testing.




TECHNICAL INFORMATION
Test methodology
	Gene Panel(s): 
	Paediatric disorders (14.43), Intellectual disability (3.2)



Whole Genome Sequencing is undertaken by Illumina and analysis of variants is prioritised by the Genomics England bioinformatics pipeline for the Genomic Medicine Service panel(s) listed above (see https://nhsgmspanelapp.genomicsengland.co.uk for panel content). Please note that the sensitivity is dependent upon the read depth coverage (further information available on request). Variant classification is performed according to ACMG and ACGS Best Practice Guidelines; Richards et al, 2015 Genet Med. 17:405-424; https://www.acgs.uk.com/quality/best-practice-guidelines/). Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics pipeline processing are undertaken by an external provider and are therefore outside of the laboratory?s UKAS scope of accreditation.




Appendix 1 ? Variant Classification
	Evidence for classification using ACMG/AMP and ACGS guidelines
(Richards et al. Genet Med. 2015. 17(5):405-24; Ellard et al. ACGS. 2020)
MPDZ (ENST00000319217.11):c.5827C>T p.(Gln1943Ter)

	
	EVIDENCE FOR PATHOGENICITY

	PVS1_VeryStrong
	This frameshift variant is predicted to result in premature termination of translation in exon 44 of the MPDZ gene. 

	PM2_Mod
	This variant has not been reported in the gnomAD database (~ 125,000 individuals)

	SUMMARY
	1x Very strong + 1x Moderate = Pathogenic
